pages.text: Sammy is a seahorse in a seagrass garden. He is a fish, but he looks different from many other fish.
Sammy swims slowly. His tiny fin wiggles fast, and that helps him move gently through the water.
Sammy has a curly tail. He wraps his tail around seagrass to hold on when waves push the water.
Seahorses can hide by blending in. Sammy tries to match the color of the plants around him.
Sammy’s body has hard bony plates. Many fish have soft scales, but seahorses have stronger armor-like plates.
Sammy uses his long snout to sip tiny food. He slurps small shrimp-like snacks floating nearby.
A big fish swims past. Sammy stays still, holding tight, and hiding among the seagrass.
Seagrass meadows help many ocean animals. They are like underwater fields where creatures find food and shelter.
Sammy remembers: hold on with your tail, swim slowly, and hide by blending in when you need safety.
When the water calms, Sammy relaxes and drifts a little. The seagrass garden waves like a soft green dance.
